newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal may pay families to have more children.
newsitem.headline: Portugal may pay families to have more children.

text.p: Portugal, worried by a falling birth rate, may pay special benefits to families that have more than two children, a minister said on Wednesday.
Social Security Minister Jorge Ferro Rodrigues said the plan was included in a package of reforms to the family welfare system the Socialist government was sending to parliament.
Rodrigues, who declined to spell out how much the government would pay, said the benefit would be extended to all families regardless of income.
"Portugal cannot afford to have such low birth levels without running the risk of becoming a country of pensioners in 30 or 40 years time," he said.
European Union figures for 1993, the latest available, show that Portugal had 11.6 births per 1,000 inhabitants against a European average of 11.0.
But National Statistics Institute officials say that the rate has been on a downward trend for years.
